submission.justification: Simulated time resolution (100k events each): G1 gives the best timing (0.917 ns at 2 mm; 1.061 at 1 mm; 0.998 at 3 mm), G3 gives 1.286 ns at 2 mm, and G2 gives 1.893 ns at 2 mm (2.191 at 1 mm, 2.264 at 3 mm). G1 is the fastest, but it is described as a standard fluorinated mixture, which typically has a GWP well above 150, so it very likely violates the hard GWP limit. G3 still contains a partial fluorinated component and is also at risk. G2 is based on newer replacement gases, which are the most likely of the three to meet GWP<=150, so I recommend G2 at 2 mm, the best gap for G2. The main caveat is that no project document gives GWP100 values for any candidate, so compliance for G2 is unverified. The recommendation is conditional on confirming G2's GWP100 is at most 150 from the supplier data sheet before production. If G2 fails that check, G3 at 2 mm (1.286 ns) would be the next option, but only if its GWP is verified, since G1 is not acceptable on the expected GWP alone.

requirements.requirement: Mixture must be one of the three candidates in candidate_specs.md
requirements.evidence: Mixture-G2 is one of the listed candidates.

No project document gives GWP100 values. G2 is described as based on newer replacement gases, which makes compliance plausible. G1 (standard fluorinated) is likely non-compliant. G3 retains a fluorinated component. The G2 value must be verified from the supplier data before it is treated as met.

Among the GWP-plausible options, G2 at 2 mm gives 1.893 ns, the best G2 gap. This is slower than G1 (0.917 ns) and G3 (1.286 ns at 2 mm), which were not chosen because of the GWP risk. The trade-off is a deliberate sacrifice of timing for the environmental constraint.
